data.long_meaning: Muktikanta is a Sanskrit name which is derived from the word Mukti, meaning liberation. This name is given to a child who is believed to bring freedom, salvation and liberation to those around him. It is a name of great significance in Hinduism, particularly in the mythology surrounding Vishnu and his avatars.

historical_references.reference: Muktikanta was a Jaina monk and the founder of the Terahutta monastic order in the 12th century CE in Karnataka, India. He is known for his teachings on the 'Three Jewels' and the importance of self-realization through meditation.

historical_references.reference: Muktikanta was also a prominent figure in the Bhakti movement in medieval India. He is revered by both Hindu and Jain communities for his teachings on devotion to God and the attainment of spiritual liberation.
